question: Thanks to the naive transfer of Western technology – European technology in the main – the People’s Republic of China began 15 years ago to roll out a strategy to develop its own domestic car industry, using state aid on a very large scale. The decision by the EU to electrify its car fleet is as naïve as transferring technology in return for market share.

China controls virtually the entire supply chain for electric cars: Chinese marques not only receive state aid on a very large scale; it also allows them sell their cars on the EU market at dumping prices.

KPMG has calculated that Chinese cars have already captured 20% of the electric vehicle market and that in two years' time, to the detriment of European carmakers, Chinese marques will account for 15% of the total EU automotive market.
China may be a member of the WTO, but it is determinedly following its own domestic political economy agenda while the EU elite still believes in the globalist fairy tale of a level playing field. 1.
Is the Commission also investigating Chinese state aid to other strategic sectors?
Has the Commission filed a complaint with the WTO in this regard?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.3.2024) The Commission is fully committed to defend EU industry from unfairly traded imports, including from China. The Commission robustly uses the trade defence instruments: currently there are 184 trade defence measures in place, 118 concern unfair and injurious imports from China - the full list can be found on DG Trade’s website1.

Where the Commission receives evidence of unfairly subsidised or dumped imports harming an EU industry it opens investigations to tackle to matter. Where it is justified, measures are imposed, generally for a period of five years, which can be extended. The Commission has also stepped-up monitoring and enforcement of the measures in place so that they are not circumvented.

In addition to the ex-officio anti-subsidy investigation which the Commission opened in October 2023 into battery electric vehicles from China, there are other anti-subsidy investigations and anti-subsidy measures in place concerning imports from that country in many different sectors – listed in the Annex attached. The European Union has not filed a complaint with the World Trade Organisation on this issue.
